title: DA vs MDA (and the 91.175 Big Three)
hook: One altitude you decide AT. One you park ON. Mix them up and the FAA writes.

scenes.narration: Thirty seconds, kid. D A versus M D A. Two little letters apart, one very different bottom of the approach.
D A — decision altitude — comes with a glidepath. You keep descending, and AT that number you decide: land or miss. You'll dip a hair below while the miss starts. That's built in.
onScreenText: Decide AT it, momentum below it

scenes.narration: M D A — minimum descent altitude — is a hard floor on a non-precision approach. Level off, hold it to the missed point, and do NOT sag below it hunting for the airport.
onScreenText: Level off. Hold it. No sagging.

scenes.narration: Going below either one takes all three: the airplane in position to land normally, the required flight visibility, and the runway environment in sight — lights, markings, threshold. All three, kid. Two out of three is a missed approach with extra steps.
D A you decide at. M D A you ride level. And the big three unlock the descent. My examiner in eighty-seven asked me all of this. I still remember his face — mostly the frown.
Ninety-one one seventy-five, paragraph c. The whole ballgame.

quiz.question: The key operational difference: at an MDA you...
choices: Level off and maintain it until landing criteria or the missed point
Descend 100 ft lower to look for the runway
quiz.explanation: MDA is a floor you hold on a non-precision approach; DA is where you decide during a continuous guided descent.

quiz.question: Descending below DA or MDA requires (14 CFR 91.175(c)):
choices: Normal-landing position + required flight visibility + runway environment in sight
quiz.explanation: All three: continuous position for a normal descent/landing, the flight visibility on the plate, and a visual reference from the 91.175(c)(3) list.

quiz.question: Seeing ONLY the approach light system, you may descend below mins but no lower than:
choices: 100 ft above touchdown zone elevation (unless red terminating/side-row bars are visible)
You may not descend at all
quiz.explanation: 91.175(c)(3)(i): approach lights alone get you to 100 ft above TDZE — lower requires the red terminating or side-row bars, or another runway reference.
